title: Broken lookup
description:
Error-prone rule — a lookup whose source no longer exists: the table occurrence is gone, the source table is missing in the target file, or the source field was deleted. A lookup that cannot resolve copies nothing and reports nothing, so the field simply stays empty on every new record.

Based on the fmCheckMate check "ListFieldsWithBrokenLookup" — https://github.com/mrwatson-de/fmCheckMate-XSLT
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: Nothing fails visibly. The field stays empty, and because a lookup only fires on entry, the gap shows up in new records long after the change that caused it.
rule.remediation: Point the lookup at an existing field, or drop the lookup if the value is now supplied elsewhere.

meta.name: Broken lookup
meta.author: fm-lab rules
meta.description: Error-prone rule — a lookup whose source no longer exists: the table occurrence is gone, the source table is missing in the target file, or the source field was deleted. A lookup that cannot resolve copies nothing and reports nothing, so the field simply stays empty on every new record.
meta.calibration: Deliberately not built on dangling UUIDs: cross-file references routinely carry a stale UUID while the target is intact — FileMaker caches foreign UUIDs but resolves through the id at runtime — so a UUID-based check reports mostly healthy references (measured on a large solution: 97 % false positives on the comparable layout-reference check). The chain used here is table occurrence → base table → resolved data-source file → field, with lookups into files outside the export counted as unverifiable rather than broken.

params.name: file
params.description: Optional file filter (from the app-level filter).

messages.missing-relationship: Lookup points at a table occurrence that no longer exists
messages.missing-table: Lookup source table does not exist in the target file
messages.missing-field: Lookup source field does not exist in the source table
